architecture.mechanism: Multithreaded two-stage filtering combining analytical constraint verification with physical intersection detection
architecture.intervention: Implement a real-time two-stage filter in the engine control unit where the first stage analytically validates commanded throttle and deceleration trajectories against stroke and angular constraints, and the second stage uses physics-based simulation to detect mechanical interference states that cause vibration-induced unintended acceleration before executing actuator commands.
architecture.expected_effect: Unintended acceleration events during deceleration are blocked by rejecting invalid actuator configurations prior to execution, preserving normal deceleration and idle operation without triggering diagnostic warning lights because the filtering occurs within standard control loop parameters.
architecture.falsification_test: Command a deceleration profile known to induce vibration-related unintended acceleration in the baseline system; if the two-stage filter allows the anomalous throttle command to pass and the vehicle accelerates for any duration, the intervention is falsified.
